clue.text: Wealthy after ring with stone for bird

indicators.note: after places the word for wealthy behind the ring and stone pieces

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight
wealthy means rich

explanation.surface: A rich man trades a jewelled ring for a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The ostrich is a large flightless African bird, the biggest living species.

clue.text: Slow motion over circle — Newton's a wise man

indicators.note: over here means covering or spanning, so the slow-motion piece goes over the circle and holds it

parts.note: slo-mo is the informal short form of slow motion
a circle is shaped like the letter O
N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force

explanation.surface: Replaying Isaac Newton in slow motion shows him to be a sage.
explanation.walkthrough: Newton tempts you towards physics, but he only supplies N, the symbol of the unit of force.
explanation.definitionFit: King Solomon of the Bible is proverbial for wisdom, so his name serves for any sage.

clue.text: Stable workhorse when reared conceals this wheel

indicators.note: a horse that rears stands up, and in a down clue going up means reading backwards
conceals says the answer lies hidden inside the words stable workhorse

explanation.surface: A dependable carthorse rearing up hides a piece of riding kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conceals' hides LEWOR across 'StabLE WORkhorse'; 'when reared' turns it upwards. The clue is self-referential: the wheel is the one hidden in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowel is the small spiked wheel at the end of a rider's spur, used to urge a horse on.

clue.text: CIA informer hides nothing entering country

indicators.note: hides means the agency's letters wrap around the rest

parts.note: taken as written: the American intelligence agency

indicators.note: entering puts the nothing piece inside the informer word

parts.note: a rat is slang for an informer
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: An American spy agency shelters an informant arriving in a Balkan state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'informer' suggests a spy story to go with the CIA, but it is just slang for a rat; 'entering' and 'hides' nest the pieces one inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Croatia is a Balkan republic on the Adriatic coast, once part of Yugoslavia.

clue.text: Cut TV host with irritating chat show — how they begin returning!

indicators.note: returning means the whole assembled run is read backwards

parts.note: Jonathan Ross is a British chat-show host

indicators.note: how they begin points to the opening letters of the three words before it

explanation.surface: Axe the television presenter with the annoying talk programme, the clue jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: Jonathan Ross is a well-known British television chat-show host. 'how they begin' takes ICS from the initials; 'returning' turns ROSSICS backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To scissor is to cut with scissors, so the verb matches the clue's opening word.

clue.text: Double lives after credit crunch

indicators.note: after puts the doubled piece behind the credit abbreviation

parts.note: CR is the standard abbreviation for credit in accounts

indicators.note: double says the lives word appears twice in a row

parts.note: lives means is, as in exists

explanation.surface: Someone leading a double life after the credit crunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'credit crunch' looks like one phrase, but the clue splits it: 'credit' gives CR and 'crunch' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A crunch is a decisive moment of difficulty, which is just what an emergency or turning point is.

clue.text: Second one missing from 13's bad type

indicators.note: bad signals that the remaining letters are jumbled
missing from says the one piece is taken out of what follows

parts.note: 13 is FRIESIAN, the answer to 13-across, and its possessive supplies a final S
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: With one character dropped, the cow from another clue becomes faulty printing.
explanation.walkthrough: Take S plus FRIESIANS, remove I ('missing from'), and 'bad' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A sans serif is a typeface whose letters lack the small finishing strokes called serifs.

clue.text: Hole left golfer, without hesitation, blocked by one tree

indicators.note: blocked by says the one piece sits inside, plugging the rest

parts.note: a hole is round, the letter O

indicators.note: without says the hesitation sound is removed from the golfer's name

parts.note: Arnold Palmer was a famous American golfer
er is the sound of hesitation
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A golfer misses a hole on the left because a tree is in the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes ER from PALMER, giving PALM; 'blocked by' puts I into O, L, PALM. The golfing picture is misdirection: Palmer is just the golfer's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The oil palm is a tropical tree whose fruit yields palm oil.

clue.text: False boobs, big cups, topless, squeezed — this male, when picked up, will return

definitions.text: this male, when picked up, will return

indicators.note: boobs as a verb means blunders, so the word false is botched into a new order

parts.note: DD is a large bra cup size

indicators.note: topless says the first letter is removed

parts.note: squeezed means pressed

explanation.surface: A cheeky description of a glamour model's enhanced figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boobs' looks like a noun, but is a verb meaning blunders and signals the anagram of FALSE. 'male, when picked up' sounds like mail: a stamped addressed envelope comes back to its sender.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-addressed envelope carries the sender's own address, so the post returns it to them.

clue.text: Famous last words initially covering a weakness

indicators.note: covering says the initials wrap around the letter A
initially takes the first letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: A celebrity's dying words reveal a fault.
explanation.definitionFit: A flaw is a defect or failing, a weak point in something or someone.

clue.text: Womble advice — one telly oddly discarded in a well-trained fashion

indicators.note: the letters in odd positions of the run of words are thrown away, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: A Womble's tip about getting rid of the television.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wombles are furry litter-picking creatures from a British children's TV show. Run 'Womble advice one telly' together and keep its 2nd, 4th, 6th... letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing as you are told is how a well-trained dog or pupil behaves.

clue.text: Charm of an '80s hairdo with only one length

parts.note: an gives the single letter A

indicators.note: with only one says one of the two matching letters is dropped

parts.note: the mullet, short at the front and long at the back, was a 1980s haircut

explanation.surface: A lucky charm made from a 1980s hairstyle trimmed down.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a charm worn to ward off evil or bring luck.

clue.text: Milk deliverer, endlessly fast Ernie's off with one

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged
endlessly applies to both fast and Ernie, cutting the last letter from each word

parts.note: both words taken as written, each then losing its final letter
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Ernie, the fastest milkman in the West, goes off with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Benny Hill's song 'Ernie (The Fastest Milkman in the West)' sets the scene. 'endlessly' trims both words to FAS and ERNI; 'off' shuffles them with I.
explanation.definitionFit: A Friesian is a black-and-white dairy cow, and a cow is what delivers milk in the first place.

clue.text: Do they keep writing stuff in back of book at stations?

indicators.note: back of takes the final letter of the word book

parts.note: stations such as taxi ranks are stands

explanation.surface: A question about whether you keep scribbling inside a book at railway stations.
explanation.definitionFit: Inkstands are desk stands holding ink pots and pens, so they hold the writing materials.

clue.text: Instruction to keep a male snake inside vessel

indicators.note: to keep says the instruction word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: stet is a proofreader's instruction meaning let it stand
a boa is a large constricting snake

explanation.surface: Orders for stowing a male snake aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: STET is the editing mark meaning keep the original text, cancelling a correction.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamboat is a steam-powered boat, a type of vessel.

clue.text: Councillor that is protecting main character in Miami Vice

indicators.note: protecting says the that-is letters surround the next piece

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: main character in means the first letter of Miami

explanation.surface: A local politician covering up for the star of a 1980s cop show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miami Vice' reads as the TV show, but the clue splits it: 'Vice' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Vice in the police sense means criminal activity, so the squad name stands for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Hope Supertramp agree finally to reform for something almost out of this world

definitions.text: something almost out of this world

indicators.note: to reform means to form again, so the letters are rearranged
finally takes the last letter of the word agree

explanation.surface: Fans hope the band Supertramp will agree to get back together.
explanation.walkthrough: Supertramp is a rock band, and a nod to the setter Tramp.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper atmosphere lies at the edge of space, so it is nearly but not quite beyond the Earth.

clue.text: Record recalled flower — it might be from Paris?

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the record letters are turned round

parts.note: LP, a long-playing record
the aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: A record recalls a flower, perhaps one from Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from Paris' suggests something French, but the answer is plaster of Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaster of Paris is a quick-setting gypsum plaster, named after the gypsum quarries near the French capital.

clue.text: Meal from a KFC mostly coating finest piece of chicken? On the contrary

indicators.note: coating says one piece wraps around the other
on the contrary reverses which piece wraps which

parts.note: the breast is the choicest meat on a chicken

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: the letters of a KFC

explanation.surface: Fast-food chicken in batter makes a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the shortened KFC would coat the chicken; 'On the contrary' flips that, so the chicken piece goes round the fast-food letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Breakfast is the first meal of the day.

clue.text: Most sharp copper intervening during a trial

indicators.note: intervening during says the copper symbol goes inside the trial piece

parts.note: a trial is a test, with the a kept
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A police officer interrupts a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer, but it is the metal, symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: Acute means sharp, as in keen or pointed, so its superlative is the sharpest.

clue.text: Criminal tie with sins relating to any of five popes

definitions.text: relating to any of five popes

indicators.note: criminal suggests something wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wrongdoing and sins linked to a series of pontiffs.
explanation.definitionFit: Five popes took the name Sixtus, and the Sistine Chapel is named after Sixtus IV.

clue.text: One advocates love with it on tart

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: with it means fashionable, hip
a tart is a pie

explanation.surface: A trendy person advocating love while eating a pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippies of the 1960s preached peace and free love.

clue.text: Free as a bird without married ones that pull in pub

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the jumbled letters wrap the married piece
free says the letters are released to form a new order

explanation.surface: Unmarried people, free as birds, go looking for partners in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' rearranges AS A BIRD into BARAIDS; 'without' (meaning outside) puts M inside. 'pull' looks like dating, but means pulling pints.
explanation.definitionFit: Barmaids pull pints of beer at the pumps in a pub.

clue.text: Highest state to take in quiet moments

indicators.note: to take in means to enclose, so the state letters wrap the other pieces

parts.note: UT is the abbreviation for Utah, a US state
p is piano, the musical direction for quiet
mos is the plural of mo, short for moment

explanation.surface: The best place to spend some quiet moments.
explanation.definitionFit: Upmost is a variant of uppermost, meaning topmost.

clue.text: Lost following international break (Man City)

indicators.note: break means the man word is split open, with the other pieces put in
following puts the lost letter after the international one

parts.note: L stands for lost in sports results

explanation.surface: Manchester City fans lament a defeat after an international break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man City' reads as Manchester City football club, but splits: 'Man' is broken into and 'City' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Milan is a major city in northern Italy, home of two big football clubs.

clue.text: See 17
Put clock back

indicators.note: back means the letters run in reverse

parts.note: dial is slang for a face, and the dial is a clock's face

explanation.surface: Turn the clock back.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid is the past tense of lay, meaning put down.

clue.text: Friar Tuck runs into trouble

indicators.note: to tuck is to slip something in, so the runs letter is tucked inside
into says the runs letter goes inside the trouble word

parts.note: bother means trouble
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Robin Hood's merry man Friar Tuck finds himself in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Friar Tuck' reads as Robin Hood's companion, but splits: 'Friar' is the definition and 'Tuck' an insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Friars are members of religious orders who address one another as brother.

clue.text: Points of view: "Primarily some things never change" — everybody speaks about America

indicators.note: about means around, so the initials surround the America letter
primarily takes the first letters of the six words that follow

explanation.surface: A maxim that nothing changes, as everybody is talking about America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primarily' gives STNCES from the initials; 'about' puts A inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Stances are attitudes or positions taken on an issue.
